- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward correction at 5–10% of spike magnitude.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model often fails to recognize it; adjust forecast to reflect 1–2% slower decline.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to reduce volatility amplification.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment direction; prioritize sentiment-weighted average over pure trend.
